# Takkāriyajātaka (Ja 481)

**ID:** Ja 481  
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Takkāriyajātaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul12.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul12.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

At the conclusion of the tale, the Buddha identifies the chaplain with Kokālika and himself with Takkāriyapaṇḍita [Fausböll 1887].

**Sources**

- [Nyanaponika et al. 2003] Nyanaponika Thera, Hellmuth Hecker, and Bhikkhu Bodhi, Great Disciples of the Buddha (2003) — Information on Kokālika's offence against Sāriputta and Moggallāna as the framing context.
- [DeCaroli 2004] Robert DeCaroli, Haunting the Buddha: Indian Popular Religions and the Formation of Buddhism (2004) — Discussion of Bharhut reliefs and scholarly identifications of the Takkāriya Jātaka.
- [Fausböll 1887] V. Fausböll, The Jātaka together with Its Commentary, Vol. 4 (1887) — Pali text, verses, story of Kokālika and the purohita, and Bodhisatta identification.
- [Fausböll 1897] V. Fausböll, The Jātaka together with Its Commentary, Vol. 7 (Index) (1897) — Attestation of the Bodhisatta as Takkāriya-paṇḍito, māṇavo in Jātaka 481.
- [Mus 1935] Paul Mus, Barabuḍur: Esquisse d'une histoire du bouddhisme fondée sur la critique archéologique des textes, part 2 — Analysis of the city-gate sacrifice motif, replacement of the brahman by a goat, and Takkāriya's role.
